title: Advancing broad implementation of genomic medicine in nephrology
text: The proposed K01 award “Advancing broad implementation of genomic medicine in nephrology” responds to the NIDDK’s research priorities related to filling a critical gap between the discovery of novel genes in nephrology and the limited utilization of those discoveries in practice; this gap prevents personalization of care of all patients with kidney diseases. To fill this gap, this study will identify barriers to genetic testing in nephrology and develop and test a point-of-care toolbox focused on genomic literacy—a key barrier for uptake of genetic testing. This K01 will prepare the candidate to develop an independent research program in implementation science and generate innovative interventions to accelerate implementation of genomic medicine in nephrology.

title: Mutant p53 in Tumorigenesis, Invasion, and Metastasis
text:
While most cancer-associated TP53 alleles disable wild type p53 function, mounting evidence suggests that 
some alleles can exhibit gain-of-function properties that influence cancer phenotypes beyond TP53 loss but 
whether, to what extent, and how TP53 mutations can have gain-of-function properties is controversial. Our 
proposal combines sophisticated genome editing, functional genomics, and mouse modeling approaches with 
innovative transcriptomic and epigenomic technologies to systematically probe the gain-of-function potential of 
hundreds of cancer-associated mutant p53 alleles in cancer, with a particular focus on those that influence 
pancreatic cancer progression and metastasis. These studies will constitute the most comprehensive foray into 
the investigation of the biology of TP53 mutants up to date and will serve as a roadmap for future studies of 
allelic variation in cancer and other diseases.

title: A developmental engineering toolbox for controlled epithelial morphogenesis
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it will study and engineer new principles of organ
development toward building functional human tissue models. Once these new principles are applied, they will
spur significant advances in tissue engineering. The proposed research is especially relevant to one of the NIH’s
2021-2025 strategic plan goals, which specifically highlights new cell engineering and bioengineering
approaches to building human tissues for disease modeling that will contribute to reducing illness and disability.

title: The Meharry Cancer Summer Research Program (SuRP)
text: Both an increased awareness of cancer burden across populations and a more comprehensive development of the cancer research/oncology workforce are required to fully address the problem of cancer within our country. The proposed Meharry Cancer Summer Research Program (SuRP) will provide undergraduate and medical students an opportunity to complete short-term, cancer focused research experiences that will enhance their understanding of the biology of cancer and cancer outcomes. It will also inspire participants to pursue careers in cancer research.

title: Role of Maternal MCM4 in Zygotic DNA Replication and Oocyte-to-Embryo Transition
text:
Proper maternal control of zygotic DNA replication is crucial for early embryonic development and fertility. This
project will investigate how loss of maternal MCM4 impairs zygotic genome duplication, disrupts mitotic fidelity,
and alters epigenetic and transcriptional dynamics in the mouse embryo. Understanding these mechanisms will
provide insight into causes of developmental arrest and inform strategies to improve reproductive outcomes.

title: Comprehensive single-cell atlas of the developing mouse brain
text:
The developing mouse brain is a foundational experimental model for investigation of the origins of cell types in
the mammalian brain and for studies of neurodevelopmental diseases. During development, the astonishing
diversity of cell types present in the adult brain is thought to be established through sequential changes in gene
expression during cellular maturation and differentiation, and further refinement with emerging brain connectivity
and function. To gain a deeper understanding of this highly complex process, we aim to combine multiple single-
cell genomics technologies to generate a comprehensive cell atlas of the developing mouse brain, intended to
serve as a first-of-its-kind foundational resource to the neuroscience community for the study of mechanisms of
mammalian brain development and neurodevelopmental disorders.

title: The Role of Nuclear Factor Erythroid 2-related factor 2 in Sarcopenic Obesity
text:
Sarcopenic obesity is strongly associated with a decline in physical function and less independence in older
adults. As such, there is immense value in determining strategies to mitigate sarcopenic obesity to improve the
quality of life in older adults. The proposed study will pave the way for novel mechanistic insights and the discovery
of new therapeutics for healthspan during aging with obesity.

title: Fred Hutchinson Breast Cancer Clinical Validation Center
text:
Despite improvements in screening and treatment, breast cancer remains the 2nd most common cause of
cancer related death among U.S. women. With current EDRN funding we conducted successful Phase 2 and 3
validation studies of breast cancer biomarkers for clearly defined clinical applications. Herein we propose
Phase 2, 3, and 4 validation studies, development of clinical grade assays, and integration of imaging data with
the goal of implementing a novel strategy to improve the early detection of breast cancer.

title: Identifying Cancer Recurrence with Novel Data Linkages with a Cancer Registry
text:
Fear of recurrence or cancer coming back is an important issue for the estimated 17 million cancer survivors
who are alive in the US today, but cancer recurrence information is currently not available for research in the
national cancer registry data due to difficulties in capturing this information. At the Utah Cancer Registry, we
have multiple statewide linkages to health records data that other registries do not have, that could facilitate
obtaining cancer recurrence data. We propose to develop methods to identify recurrence and validate the
methods with the Cancer Registry in Seattle-Puget Sound, so that other researchers can apply the methods to
data in the cancer registries and with additional data linkages that are rapidly increasing across cancer
registries in various states.

title: Transcriptional Regulation of human natural killer cell function
text:
Human cytomegalovirus has been shown to cause serious health complications in immunosuppressed
individuals and newborns. This proposal will define how a specific transcription factor, MEF2C, controls human
natural killer (NK) cell metabolism and protective responses during viral infection. A detailed understanding of
the molecular mechanisms that regulate human NK cells during viral infection may lead to novel
immunotherapies and treatment strategies for immunocompromised patients.

title: Meltblown Scaffolds for Irreparable Rotator Cuff Tears: Interposition Grafting
text:
Irreparable rotator cuff tears in the shoulder cause pain and disability and lead to shoulder osteoarthritis and
sometimes to joint replacement. Complex interposition grafting can sometimes restore function and reduce pain,
but there are no medical devices designed specifically for this purpose. In these studies, we will design and test
a new device capable of improving function better than the current dermal allograft standard of care.

title: Targeting bile acid composition to treat metabolic diseases
text:
Nearly 1 in 3 people are overweight and nearly 2 in 5 people have obesity; so, obesity is a national epidemic.
The proposed research is highly relevant to public health because new effective therapies for obesity and
obesity-related complications (e.g., NAFLD/NASH and type 2 diabetes) are needed. The tools and knowledge
gained, and the mechanistic details to be discovered in this proposal, all fit the purview of NIDDK's mission to
reduce the burden of obesity and obesity-related metabolic complications.

title: The effect of severe obesity on regional lung perfusion in acute hypoxemic respiratory failure
text:
Severe obesity is a significant risk factor for acute hypoxemic respiratory failure,
cardiopulmonary complications, and premature death. The proposed research will characterize
the effect of severe obesity on regional lung perfusion and vasoreactivity during acute
hypoxemic respiratory failure. The K23 career development award will support the training to
establish the candidate as an independent patient-oriented translational researcher in critical
care medicine.

title: Interrogate FMRP functions in primate brain development
text:
The proposed work will fill a major gap of our knowledge in understanding function of FMRP in primate brain
development. Such understanding is critical for better therapeutic development for fragile X syndrome as well as
other neurodevelopmental disorders including autism.

title: Elucidating roles of the CD24 ligand in early lung cancer development, immune evasion and response to KRAS-targeted therapy
text:
Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) with activating mutations in the KRAS oncogene is the most common molecular
subtype of lung cancer and strategies for early treatment of the disease heavily rest on unraveling targetable
changes that enable its pathogenesis. While recent advances in KRAS-targeted therapy have shown promising
results in the clinic, still, many patients with KRAS-mutant LUAD do not respond or develop resistance to KRAS
inhibition for reasons we do not fully understand. The proposed project will unravel how the tumor cell surface
ligand CD24 promotes KRAS-mutant LUAD development and immune evasion, as well as how this high-potential
target can be therapeutically leveraged in combination with KRAS inhibition to better treat LUAD.

title: Bay Area Cancer Target Discovery and Development
text:
The goal of this proposal is directly to bridge the gap between the enormous volumes of data generated
by the comprehensive molecular characterization of a number of cancer types– and the ability to use
these data for the development of human cancer therapeutics.

title: The molecular mechanisms underlying PHF6-mutation-mediated hematologic malignancies
text:
The PHF6 gene is frequently mutated and/or deleted in various hematologic
malignancies, including T-ALL, AML, MDS, and MPAL. The PHF6 mutations in
hematological malignancies are largely frameshift and nonsense, however, the impact of
PHF6 mutations in the development of hematologic malignancies remains largely
unknown. The major goal of this proposal is to address these critical knowledge gaps
using our newly developed Phf6 mutation-targeted murine models.

title: Building an “AI Forest” to identify the social and environmental factors underlying complex behavioral traits in wild primates.
text:
This project will establish a foundation for an Artificial Intelligence (AI) Forest that will transform our ability to
study non-human primates in their natural environment. This work will enable the collection of multidimensional
behavioral and environmental data that will enhance our understanding of complex brain-behavior relationships
and ultimately inform translational science.

title: Role of Glycosphingolipids in Kidney Disease in Diabetes and Obesity
text:
In this proposal we will test the hypothesis that increases in glucosylceramide composition play an important
role in the pathogenesis and progression of kidney disease in obesity and diabetes. We propose that these
lipids mediate impaired mitochondrial function and inflammation, which are important mediators of kidney
disease. In Specific Aim 1, we will determine if inhibition of glucosylceramide synthesis by employing a)
podocyte or b) renal tubule specific inducible inhibition of glucosylceramide synthase will prevent the
progression of kidney disease in mouse models of obesity and diabetes. In Specific Aim 2, we will determine
if reductions in glucosylceramide levels will improve mitochondrial function (oxidative phosphorylation and/or
fatty acid oxidation rate) and dynamics (fusion/fission and/or mitophagy). In Specific Aim 3, we will determine
if inhibition of proinflammatory TH17 cell-specific glucosylceramide synthase will decrease inflammation and
result in improved kidney function in mouse models of obesity and diabetes.

title: NIDA Center of Excellence in Omics, Systems Genetics, and the Addictome
text:
The goal of the NIDA Core Center of Excellence in Omics, Systems Genetics, and the Addictome (OSGA
Center) is to build and empower a community of substance use disorder (SUD) researchers to use large-scale
data approaches to test and confirm causal links from genetic, molecular, and cellular traits to SUD-related
behaviors in rodent models and to translate these findings to human clinical SUD prevention and treatment. We
will continue to provide researchers with the training, data resources, and analytical tools needed to integrate
data science, quantitative genetics, and AI techniques into their work, making precision medicine for SUD an
attainable goal.
